operations.value:
Handle a rejected push by replaying local operations onto the fetched remote tip instead of leaving a divergent task ref. Reuse the single auto-sync path: fetch, mutate, push, and on rejection fetch again, roll the canonical local ref back to the remote tip, park the orphaned commit under refs/workbook/reconciled/<task-id>/<n>, and replay each local-only operation pack onto the new parent as ordinary single-parent commits. Most concurrent edits touch disjoint fields, commute, and replay silently, so a losing push normally republishes without asking anything. Introduce no multi-parent commits; the single-parent tip and history rules in gitstore read and history validation stay unchanged.

Surface exactly three conflicts. Each aborts replay for that task and leaves the canonical ref at the fetched remote tip: both sides changed description; a replayed dependency set.add closes a cycle against the fetched graph; and an upstream tombstone leaves a local operation unable to apply. Report them through one conflict member in the result envelope with a type discriminator. Description carries base, ours, and theirs; dependency carries the edge and the closing path; tombstone carries the blocked operation. Never write conflict markers or any unresolved value into a commit. Resolution is a plain retry of the ordinary command against the now fast-forwarded ref, so no reconcile command, no continue command, and no persistent conflict state exist anywhere. The contract is non-interactive and complete without a terminal so JSON output, hooks, agents, and the web board all use it; TTY prompting is a later affordance layered on top.

Make retryability answerable from the exit code alone. Add a conflict category with exit code 8, meaning read the envelope, change the input, then retry. Redefine 6 stale-write to mean the opposite: retry the identical command and it will probably succeed. Divergence and rejected pushes stop reporting 6 because they now reconcile, leaving 6 to cover local ref races and validation-cache races. Reclassify the equal-rank gap error in core service from stale-write to validation, since it is not a race and fails identically on every retry; replaying a move records its literal computed rank, so two clones can converge on equal ranks and reach it more often.

Treat every other concurrent field change as silent last-syncer-wins, including a replayed operation whose value already matches upstream, which records no commit. Prune parked refs for a task inside the existing update-ref transaction on the next successful mutation of that task from this clone, never on reads or fetches, keeping at most the last few per task. Parked refs stay local and are never pushed, which the taskRefPrefix-scoped ref enumerations already provide for free.

Acceptance targets against a local bare remote at the existing 500-task by 20-operation workload: a losing push that replays silently completes within a p95 of 1500ms and fewer than 20 Git processes; a reported conflict aborts within the same budget; replay cost scales with the number of local-only operations rather than history depth; and cli-update keeps its existing 200ms budget when no rejection occurs.

Out of scope: global dependency-cycle validation, since a cycle can already appear from two clean fast-forwards on different tasks with no conflict at all, and workbook next reporting no available task is the accepted signal; bounded replay retry, which hands back on the first rejection; interactive prompting; three-way description merging, tracked separately; and any change to serve beyond consuming the same contract.
